title: Self-Application Is Not Free: the Monitoring Channel Is Part of the Failure Channel, and the Self Does Not Survive Its Own Reconstruction
description: This paper states and measures two claims. (i) The monitoring channel is part of the failure channel: a self-referential system's self-monitoring is not an instrumental probe chosen and bounded apart from the process it monitors — it IS self-reference, its cost feeds the failure variable, and every self-side instrument the programme built failed because the instrument and the thing measured share a channel. The sensor-placement rule this forced — put the sensor outside the channel it measures — is the design rule the worker was built to. (ii) The self does not survive its own reconstruction: an agent that must rebuild its self after every compaction loses the self in every cell, permanently — empty-self fraction 1.000 in 8/8 then 10/10 reconstruction cells against 0.08/0.07 in controls, at a cost of ~400,000 chars of self-directed reasoning per run and a ~21x thinking-to-output ratio, replicated to within 0.4% on the headline quantity across two independent sets. The work-score consequence, honestly, did not separate from zero: the effect halved on replication (2.26 -> 1.08) and reached p<0.05 in neither set (p=0.10, p=0.33/0.34); the finer held-out DV did not reduce variance and failed on its own terms. The mechanism replicates; the work consequence does not. The deposit carries the unified paper (paper-3.md, paper-3.pdf), the methods half (paper2/, design/), the worker's code (agent/, including the sealed held-out task suite), the pre-registration (ops/lambda/P3-PREREG.md), and the run data (runs/) from which every headline number is re-derivable.
notes: Deposit license is CC-BY-4.0, covering paper-3.md, paper-3.pdf and the companion records and notes in paper2/. The code in this repository (agent/, ops/) is additionally licensed under the MIT license (see LICENSE). No third-party quoted material is included. The repository is a SNAPSHOT of a private development tree at the revision named in SNAPSHOT. The held-out task suite definition (held-out-task-suite.json) and each task's heldout/ tests are included so the sealed evaluator can be re-run: a reader is not the agent under test, and the paper's design depends on the agent not reading them, not on a public reader not reading them.
